headline: A 35% volume step-up lands cleanly, with easy-run HR dropping markedly — aerobic efficiency is moving in the right direction.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The recent block represents a meaningful load increase that the body appears to have absorbed well. Easy-run HR has dropped noticeably compared to the prior period on comparable efforts — that's a concrete aerobic adaptation signal, not noise. Combined with a substantial volume step-up and stronger strength consistency, this is a block where multiple markers are pointing the same direction.

The 20-week running streak ties your personal best, which is worth acknowledging not as a milestone for its own sake but as evidence of the structural consistency that underlies these adaptations. Streaks are a trailing indicator of discipline; the HR and volume data are the leading indicators that matter more.

The lactate threshold data point from yesterday — a single test, so treat it as a baseline anchor rather than a trend — gives you a reference to compare against as more history accumulates. Watch how easy-run HR continues to evolve over the coming weeks relative to it.
watch_items: Monitor whether the easy-run HR decline continues at comparable paces, or stabilises — either outcome is informative
With a 35% volume step-up just completed, pay attention to how legs feel on the first long or quality effort of this new week
Lactate threshold is currently a single data point — note subjective feel and HR response on threshold-adjacent efforts so the picture builds faster
Strength streak is three weeks; watch whether session quality holds as running load remains elevated

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 168 km vs 125 km prior block (+35%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 144 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 6 runs)
